items.title: Jimmy Lewis interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: We had Wardell Gray, Clark Terry, Gus Johnson on drums, Freddie Green on guitar, me on bass and like we used Bud DeFranco playing tenor.

ctx.x: Is this when Basie had the small group?
Yes, the small group. We had Wardell Gray, Clark Terry, Gus Johnson on drums, Freddie Green on guitar, me on bass and like we used Bud DeFranco playing tenor.
Can I read something that Joe Williams said about that group?

items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The group started out with Basie, Gus Johnson on drums, Jimmie Lewis, who is a bass violin player that we had run into in Louisville, Kentucky, and Freddie Green, of course, guitar. In the front line was me, Buddy DeFranco, and a saxophone player.

ctx.x: . . . a bigger part of the fee.

They wanted to get Basie out of debt, so they put a small band around him, paid him a small salary. As a matter of fact, Buddy DeFranco, the clarinet player – caucasian cat. You know who he is – he was making more money than Basie was, and they put him in Basie’s band. The group started out with Basie, Gus Johnson on drums, Jimmie Lewis, who is a bass violin player that we had run into in Louisville, Kentucky, and Freddie Green, of course, guitar. In the front line was me, Buddy DeFranco, and a saxophone player.…
